key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni–20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% relative to bare SA516 boiler steel, delivering the best performance among the tested coatings.
engineering_relevance: These coatings could improve the oxidation resistance of SA516 boiler components exposed to high temperatures.
method: Apply Ni–20Cr, Ni–20Cr+40TiC, and Ni–20Cr+40TiN coatings by HVOF and plasma spraying.
Characterize microstructure and phases using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: Laboratory testing linked improved oxidation resistance to reduced porosity, enhanced microhardness, and protective oxides including Cr₂O₃, TiO₂, NiTiO₄, and NiO.
watch_item: Performance over 50 laboratory air-oxidation cycles does not establish long-term durability in corrosive, mechanically loaded boiler service.
paper_title: Microstructure and high-temperature oxidation behaviour of HVOF and plasma sprayed Ni–Cr-based ceramic coatings on SA516 boiler steel
